title: AES-GCM decrypt: AAD silently dropped when authInSz > 256, authentication runs without AAD
description:
Trigger: wc_AesGcmDecrypt called with authIn != NULL and authInSz > CRYPTO2DEV_AAD_MAXLEN (256 bytes).

In crypto2dev_cipher(), the SET_AAD ioctl is skipped when authInSz > 256:
  if (authIn != NULL && authInSz > 0 && authInSz <= CRYPTO2DEV_AAD_MAXLEN) { /* set AAD */ }

If authInSz exceeds the limit, the FINALIZE ioctl runs with no AAD set. The device authenticates the ciphertext against an empty AAD. An attacker who modifies the AAD (e.g., TLS record header fields) goes undetected if their modified AAD is still > 256 bytes.

Standard TLS AADs are 5–13 bytes so this cannot be triggered via TLS. It would affect any non-TLS caller using AES-GCM with AAD > 256 bytes (e.g., file encryption, custom protocols).

The encrypt path has the same silent skip: SET_AAD is not issued for oversized AAD, so the tag is computed over empty AAD. A subsequently decrypting party using a correct implementation will correctly reject the ciphertext, but a second crypto2dev instance would incorrectly accept it.

Fix: Return BUFFER_E (not CRYPTOCB_UNAVAILABLE) when authInSz > CRYPTO2DEV_AAD_MAXLEN, so the caller gets an explicit error rather than a silently degraded security guarantee.
